8.. Presentation/Update from the Sheriff's Department Regarding Public Safety in the City of Commerce Sergeant Mayra Duarte provided an update for the last two weeks. Vice Mayor Argumedo asked for an update about the burglary that occurred on Gaspar avenue and inquired about the status of the catalytic converter prevention campaign. Sergeant Duarte stated that staff is working on a flyer regarding catalytic converters, including information on what vehicles are mostly targeted and also preventive measures to protect from theft. There will be flyers on the upcoming Citadel drive that will be distributed to the residents.

12.. Tree Maintenance Services Agreement Extension  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Ivan Altamirano Acting Public Works Director Nila provided an overview of the staff report.  

Vice Mayor Argumedo inquired whether the tree shoots could be addressed.  According to Acting Director Nila, tree trimming is performed once a year and contract does not include returning of the contractor to address the shoots, and if the City requests the service it would be at an additional cost.  Victor Gonzales, Vice President of the West Coast Arborist, added that the company is aware of those issues of shoots coming out, but they have the capability and by working with staff to identify those areas that are more susceptible to those tree shoots, and they could place treatment on trees to prevent shoots from coming or come to those area to cut those shoots.  Mr. Gonzalez also added that the West Coast Arborist has that data on those areas that need tree shoots trimmed and could address those areas.  In response to Councilmember Altamirano's suggestion to trim while West Coast Arborist comes for watering,  Mr. Gonzales stated that they could include that as well.  

Councilmember Garcia inquired as to how often the maintenance on trees is performed, to which Director Nila responded trees are inspected annually or bi-annually depending on species. Councilmember Garcia asked about efforts made to falling/leaning trees, especially some trees currently on Eastern and Gage Avenue. According to Director Nila, small leaning trees are re-staked, and all trees are inspected annually or bi-annually and replaced if needed. However, the in-house Arborist inspects trees on an ongoing basis and staff requests West Coast Arborist address matters as needed.

Further discussion took place with leaning and falling trees. Councilmember Lainez suggested to approve the extension, direct staff to release RFP and include  hazardous evaluation component and  a la carte service.  

Acting Director Nila added that in the last ten years, the City issued RFP, had two other companies for some time, but majority of the time, West Coast Arborist was selected by the City Council.  Acting Director Nila also added that sometimes City utilizes parks maintenance staff to help with pruning of trees, and identifying hazardous areas.  

Mayor Rebollo recommended option 2 and maybe extend the contract for only six months.   


11.. Metro Measure R Funding Agreement for Slauson Corridor Improvements from I-5 to I-710 Project  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Kevin Lainez Acting Public Works Director Nila provided an overview of the staff report.

10.. Council Meeting Schedule - Cancelling December 27, 2022, Meeting and Rescheduling January 10, 2023, to January 12, 2023, due to Holiday Closure of the City Hall City Manager Cisneros provided a brief overview of the staff report.  

9.. Committee and Commission Appointments  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Hugo Argumedo Vice Mayor Argumedo appointed Daniel Reyes to Youth Advisory Commission.

Mayor Rebollo asked staff to discuss with Casino representatives continuous commitment to programs and services and see if the Casino could make any additional contributions to City programs. City Manager Cisneros stated that they would bring the ordinance for the second reading on December 13, and the City Council has until December 21, 2022, to pull the measure and call off the Special election. 


CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Mayor and Councilmembers wished everyone Happy Thanksgiving. Mayor and Councilmembers complimented the staff for working as a team on the Turkey Giveaway event. 

Councilmember Altamirano asked people to take precautions for Christmas and not leave gifts in the cars. Councilmember Altamirano asked that the staff invites Congresswoman for a meet and greet with the City. 

Councilmember Lainez reported that he attended the Parks Master Plan Workshop at Rosewood park and invited everyone to the Tree Lightening ceremony. 

Councilmember Garcia reported attending several water polo games, a holiday drive-through, and a Parks Master Plan workshop. 

Mayor Rebollo thanked staff for a great event for the seniors at the Senior Center.
